sentences.quote: If you are in the trade or business of providing foster care, your unreimbursed expenses aren’t considered support provided by you.

If you aren’t in the trade or business of providing foster care and your unreimbursed out-of-pocket expenses in caring for a foster child were mainly to benefit an organization qualified to receive deductible charitable contributions, the expenses are deductible as charitable contributions but aren’t considered support you provided.
The year you provide the support is the year you pay for it, even if you do so with borrowed money that you repay in a later year.
The allotment of pay and the tax-exempt basic allowance for quarters are both considered as provided by you for support.
In figuring a person’s total support, include tax-exempt income, savings, and borrowed amounts used to support that person.
If spouses each receive benefits that are paid by one check made out to both of them, half of the total paid is considered to be for the support of each spouse, unless they can show otherwise.

If you make a lump-sum advance payment to a home for the aged to take care of your relative for life and the payment is based on that person’s life expectancy, the amount of support you provide each year is the lump-sum payment divided by the relative’s life expectancy.
Total support includes amounts spent to provide food, lodging, clothing, education, medical and dental care, recreation, transportation, and similar necessities.
Expenses not directly related to any one member of a household, such as the cost of food for the household, must be divided among the members of the household.
If you live with a person rent free in that person’s home, you must reduce the amount you provide for support of that person by the fair rental value of lodging the person provides you.
The total fair rental value of a person’s home that the person owns is considered support contributed by that person.
Property provided as support is measured by its fair market value.
Capital items, such as furniture, appliances, and cars, bought for a person during the year can be included in total support under certain circumstances.
Medical insurance premiums you pay, including premiums for supplementary Medicare coverage, are included in the support you provide.
Medical insurance benefits, including basic and supplementary Medicare benefits, aren’t part of support.
Amounts veterans receive under the GI Bill for tuition payments and allowances while they attend school are included in total support.

If you pay someone to provide child or dependent care, you can include these payments in the amount you provided for the support of your child or disabled dependent, even if you claim a credit for the payments.
Federal, state, and local income taxes paid by persons from their own income.
Social security and Medicare taxes paid by persons from their own income.
Life insurance premiums.
Funeral expenses.
Survivors’ and Dependents’ Educational Assistance payments used for the support of the child who receives them.

claims.why_uncovered: The question gives instructions for TANF, lodging, military allotments, own funds, foster payments, the child's wages, state benefits and scholarships. A filer answering yes or no gets no guidance on these rules, and no refusal applies.

claims.quote: In figuring a person’s total support, include tax-exempt income, savings, and borrowed amounts used to support that person. / Total support includes amounts spent to provide food, lodging, clothing, education, medical and dental care, recreation, transportation, and similar necessities. / The total fair rental value of a person’s home that the person owns is considered support contributed by that person. / Capital items, such as furniture, appliances, and cars, bought for a person during the year can be included in total support under certain circumstances. / Medical insurance benefits, including basic and supplementary Medicare benefits, aren’t part of support. / Amounts veterans receive under the GI Bill for tuition payments and allowances while they attend school are included in total support. / Federal, state, and local income taxes paid by persons from their own income. / Social security and Medicare taxes paid by persons from their own income. / Survivors’ and Dependents’ Educational Assistance payments used for the support of the child who receives them.
claims.why_uncovered: The self-support question covers own funds actually spent, lodging, foster payments, scholarships and social security. It omits borrowed or tax-exempt funds, an owned home, capital purchases, GI Bill amounts, and the items excluded from support. These rules can move a child across the over-half line in the qualifying child test.

sentences.quote: For this purpose, a person isn’t a taxpayer if the person isn’t required to file a U.S. income tax return and either doesn’t file such a return or files only to get a refund of withheld income tax or estimated tax paid.

A child isn’t the qualifying child of any other taxpayer and so may qualify as your qualifying relative if the child’s parent (or other person for whom the child is defined as a qualifying child) isn’t required to file an income tax return and either: • Doesn’t file an income tax return, or • Files a return only to get a refund of income tax withheld or estimated tax paid.
If the persons the child does live with aren’t U.S. citizens and have no U.S. gross income, those persons aren’t “taxpayers,” so the child isn’t the qualifying child of any other taxpayer.

claims.quote: For this purpose, a person isn’t a taxpayer if the person isn’t required to file a U.S. income tax return and either doesn’t file such a return or files only to get a refund of withheld income tax or estimated tax paid. / A child isn’t the qualifying child of any other taxpayer and so may qualify as your qualifying relative if the child’s parent (or other person for whom the child is defined as a qualifying child) isn’t required to file an income tax return and either: • Doesn’t file an income tax return, or • Files a return only to get a refund of income tax withheld or estimated tax paid. / If the persons the child does live with aren’t U.S. citizens and have no U.S. gross income, those persons aren’t “taxpayers,” so the child isn’t the qualifying child of any other taxpayer.
claims.why_uncovered: The only related question, dependent.other_claimant, asks whether the person meets the conditions to be the qualifying child of any other person, with no carve-out for someone who is not a taxpayer. No question asks whether the other person has a filing requirement or files only for a refund, and qualifying_relative lists no refusal on this condition. The child of a non-filing friend or a parent abroad may therefore be misclassified.

sentences.quote: If you file a joint return, the person can be related to either you or your spouse.
Also, the person doesn’t need to be related to the spouse who provides support.
However, if you and your spouse file separate returns, your spouse’s stepparent can be your qualifying relative only if the stepparent lives with you all year as a member of your household.

claims.quote: If you file a joint return, the person can be related to either you or your spouse. / Also, the person doesn’t need to be related to the spouse who provides support. / However, if you and your spouse file separate returns, your spouse’s stepparent can be your qualifying relative only if the stepparent lives with you all year as a member of your household.
claims.why_uncovered: The question asks only for the relationship to you. It does not tell a joint filer to count a relationship to the spouse, such as a spouse's stepparent or a spouse's aunt. Such a person would be entered as other and would fail the test unless they lived with the filer all year.

sentences.quote: The same is true if the child lived with you more than half the year except for any required hospital stay following birth.
The test is also met if a child lived with you as a member of your household except for any required hospital stay following birth.
If the person is placed in a nursing home for an indefinite period of time to receive constant medical care, the absence may be considered temporary.
It must be reasonable to assume the absent person will return to the home after the temporary absence.
You must continue to keep up the home during the absence.

claims.quote: The same is true if the child lived with you more than half the year except for any required hospital stay following birth. / The test is also met if a child lived with you as a member of your household except for any required hospital stay following birth. / If the person is placed in a nursing home for an indefinite period of time to receive constant medical care, the absence may be considered temporary. / It must be reasonable to assume the absent person will return to the home after the temporary absence. / You must continue to keep up the home during the absence.
claims.why_uncovered: The months question lists temporary absences and gives birth, death and placement rules. It does not address a required hospital stay after birth, an indefinite nursing home placement, or the conditions that the person is expected to return and the home is kept up during the absence.

sentences.quote: Students who work on “co-op” jobs in private industry as a part of a school’s regular course of classroom and practical training are considered full-time students.
A full-time student is a student who is enrolled for the number of hours or courses the school considers to be full-time attendance.

claims.quote: Students who work on “co-op” jobs in private industry as a part of a school’s regular course of classroom and practical training are considered full-time students. / A full-time student is a student who is enrolled for the number of hours or courses the school considers to be full-time attendance.
claims.why_uncovered: The question defines the 5-month test and which schools count. It does not treat vocational co-op students as full-time, and it does not say that the school's own standard determines full-time attendance. A co-op student could be answered as not full-time.

sentences.quote: A custodial parent who has revoked their previous release of a claim to certain tax benefits for a child must include a copy of the revocation with their return.
For the revocation to be effective for 2025, the custodial parent must have given (or made reasonable efforts to give) written notice of the revocation to the noncustodial parent in 2024 or earlier.

claims.quote: A custodial parent who has revoked their previous release of a claim to certain tax benefits for a child must include a copy of the revocation with their return. / For the revocation to be effective for 2025, the custodial parent must have given (or made reasonable efforts to give) written notice of the revocation to the noncustodial parent in 2024 or earlier.
claims.why_uncovered: The question and its refusal address a release or decree that lets the noncustodial parent claim the child. Nothing asks about a revoked release, so a custodial parent could answer no and proceed. That answer would not test whether notice was timely or require the revocation copy.

sentences.quote: Child support payments aren't qualified expenses.
Generally, if you worked or actively looked for work during only part of the period in which you incurred the expenses, you must figure your expenses for each day.
Also, if part of an expense is work related (for either household services or the care of a qualifying person) and part is for other purposes, you have to divide the expense.
However, they don't include the services of a chauffeur, bartender, or gardener.

claims.quote: Child support payments aren't qualified expenses. / Generally, if you worked or actively looked for work during only part of the period in which you incurred the expenses, you must figure your expenses for each day. / Also, if part of an expense is work related (for either household services or the care of a qualifying person) and part is for other purposes, you have to divide the expense. / However, they don't include the services of a chauffeur, bartender, or gardener.
claims.why_uncovered: The long exclusion list in the question omits child support payments and the services of a chauffeur, bartender or gardener. It also omits the daily proration for part-period work and the division of mixed-purpose expenses. The phrase so that you could work or look for work does not tell the filer to make either calculation.

sentences.quote: Don’t claim the American opportunity credit for 2 years after there was a final determination that your claim was due to reckless or intentional disregard of the rules or 10 years after there was a final determination that your claim was due to fraud.

If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error for any tax year beginning after 2015, you must attach a completed Form 8862, Information To Claim Certain Credits After Disallowance, to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit.

claims.quote: Don’t claim the American opportunity credit for 2 years after there was a final determination that your claim was due to reckless or intentional disregard of the rules or 10 years after there was a final determination that your claim was due to fraud. / If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error for any tax year beginning after 2015, you must attach a completed Form 8862, Information To Claim Certain Credits After Disallowance, to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit.
claims.why_uncovered: This item is built from lines 23 to 26, filer TINs and the institution's EIN. No question or refusal here or in the handled-elsewhere list addresses the 2-year or 10-year ban or the Form 8862 requirement after a prior disallowance.

sentences.quote: Also, the American opportunity credit isn’t allowed on either your original or an amended 2025 return for a student who hasn’t been issued a TIN by the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions).
The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions).

claims.quote: Also, the American opportunity credit isn’t allowed on either your original or an amended 2025 return for a student who hasn’t been issued a TIN by the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions). / The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions).
claims.why_uncovered: The only TIN input is dependent.tin, which also answers yes when an ITIN or ATIN has merely been applied for by the due date. That is the Form 1040 Step 3 and Step 5 standard. The education credits require the TIN to have been issued by the due date, and nothing separates a pending application from an issued number.

sentences.quote: Under proposed Treasury regulations, if you received Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) payments or other similar payments and used the payment to support another person, those payments are considered support you provided for that person, rather than support provided by the government or other third party.

claims.quote: Under proposed Treasury regulations, if you received Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) payments or other similar payments and used the payment to support another person, those payments are considered support you provided for that person, rather than support provided by the government or other third party.
claims.why_uncovered: The question spells out which costs count and says funds received in a household member's name, such as Social Security, count as paid by that person. It does not say that TANF or similar payments used to support another person count as provided by the filer. A filer who paid household costs with TANF could wrongly answer No, and no other line, question or refusal addresses these payments.

sentences.quote: Under proposed Treasury regulations, if you received Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) payments or other similar payments and used the payment to support another person, those payments are considered support you provided for that person, rather than support provided by the government or other third party.
If the child isn’t claimed as your dependent, enter the child’s name in the entry space.

claims.quote: Under proposed Treasury regulations, if you received Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) payments or other similar payments and used the payment to support another person, those payments are considered support you provided for that person, rather than support provided by the government or other third party. / If the child isn’t claimed as your dependent, enter the child’s name in the entry space.
claims.why_uncovered: Test 4 of the question lists the included and excluded costs and treats a household member's own funds as paid by that member, but it omits the TANF rule. The encoding also has no line or question that captures the name of a qualifying child who is not claimed as a dependent, so the required entry is not produced.

sentences.quote: If the child isn’t claimed as your dependent, enter the child’s name in the entry space below qualifying surviving spouse.

claims.quote: If the child isn’t claimed as your dependent, enter the child’s name in the entry space below qualifying surviving spouse.
claims.why_uncovered: The encoding decides head of household eligibility, but no line or question captures the name of a qualifying child who is not claimed as a dependent. The required filing status entry is therefore not produced.

sentences.quote: Don’t file Form 8862 if you filed Form 8862 for 2024, and the child tax credit, additional child tax credit, or credit for other dependents was allowed for that year.
But don’t file Form 8862 if either of the following applies.
You filed Form 8862 for another year, the EIC was allowed for that year, and your EIC hasn’t been reduced or disallowed again for any reason other than a math or clerical error.

You are taking the EIC without a qualifying child and the only reason your EIC was reduced or disallowed in the other year was because it was determined that a child listed on Schedule EIC wasn’t your qualifying child.

If your CTC, ACTC, or ODC for a year after 2015 was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error, you must attach Form 8862 to your tax return to claim the CTC, ACTC, or ODC unless an exception applies.

claims.quote: Don’t file Form 8862 if you filed Form 8862 for 2024, and the child tax credit, additional child tax credit, or credit for other dependents was allowed for that year. / But don’t file Form 8862 if either of the following applies. / You filed Form 8862 for another year, the EIC was allowed for that year, and your EIC hasn’t been reduced or disallowed again for any reason other than a math or clerical error. / You are taking the EIC without a qualifying child and the only reason your EIC was reduced or disallowed in the other year was because it was determined that a child listed on Schedule EIC wasn’t your qualifying child. / If your CTC, ACTC, or ODC for a year after 2015 was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error, you must attach Form 8862 to your tax return to claim the CTC, ACTC, or ODC unless an exception applies.
claims.why_uncovered: The question is answered Yes for any past reduction or disallowance not due to a math or clerical error, and it has no carve-out for the listed Form 8862 exceptions. A filer who fits an exception answers Yes just like a filer who must attach Form 8862, and no other question separates the two groups.
